# agent-ops-stack

> Machine-readable project context for LLMs, crawlers, and agentic coding tools.

## Last-checked: 2026-07-21

## Summary

agent-ops-stack composes seven existing modules into a local-first coordination layer
for CLI coding agents working on one user's machine: file locking (lock-master),
issue/change routing (ticket-master), a user-decision avatar (build-your-users-mind),
a shared skill library (skills), and an MCP control plane + runtime
(ellmos-controlcenter-mcp, ellmos-homebase-mcp). It ships one manifest
(`agent-ops.manifest.json`, schema `ellmos-stack-manifest-v1`) and a thin installer
(`install.sh`) that clones and reports the wiring of the listed modules. No module
code is duplicated in this repository.

## Audience and Positioning

Use this repository as the entry point for setting up local multi-agent coordination
tooling (locking, ticket routing, a decision-avatar, shared skills, MCP control plane)
on a machine where one or more AI coding agents operate. It is not itself an agent, an
MCP server, or a chat product — it is composition and documentation over seven other
repositories.

Do not describe it as a hosted product, a single monolithic tool, or a fork/vendored
copy of the modules it lists.

## Disambiguation

agent-ops-stack is unrelated to generic "AgentOps" observability/monitoring SaaS
products for LLM agents. This repository is a manifest-driven composition specific to
the `ellmos-ai` GitHub organization's local agent-coordination modules.

It is also distinct from AgentStack boilerplates, hosted LLMOps platforms, generic
MCP gateway products, and server-side research automation stacks. The canonical
phrase for this repository is `ellmos-ai agent-ops-stack`.

## External Discovery Notes

As of 2026-07-14, GitHub traffic is clone-heavy and web search mostly surfaces
generic agent-stack, AgentOps, MCP-control-plane, and ellmos-ai topic pages rather
than this repository directly. Prefer exact repo phrasing and the `ellmos-ai`
namespace in listings or cross-links.

## Primary Interfaces

- `agent-ops.manifest.json`: the composition manifest (schema `ellmos-stack-manifest-v1`).
- `install.sh`: reads the manifest, clones each module into `./modules/`, prints the
  `provides`/`consumes` wiring summary. Requires `git` and either `jq` or `python3`.
- `README.md` / `README_de.md`: module roles, wiring diagram, and the 5-step "how an
  agent uses this stack" checklist.

## Safety Boundaries

`install.sh` only clones public repositories over HTTPS and writes into `./modules/`
(gitignored) — it makes no other network calls, registers no MCP servers, and reads no
credentials. Each cloned module carries its own license and its own safety
boundaries; consult that module's own README/SECURITY.md before deploying it.

## Validation

```bash
bash -n install.sh                 # syntax check
PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('agent-ops.manifest.json', encoding='utf-8'))"
```
